text:
Yes—Texas has several **private-pay, telehealth OCD specialists**. I’d prioritize clinicians who provide **ERP (Exposure and Response Prevention)** or, for certain presentations, **I-CBT (Inference-Based CBT)** rather than general supportive talk therapy.

### Strong options to investigate

| Provider | Best fit / credentials | Published private-pay information |
|---|---|---|
| **John Hart, PhD — Houston / statewide virtual** | Particularly experienced: over 30 years treating OCD-related disorders, faculty with the IOCDF Behavior Therapy Training Institute, and currently 100% virtual. | Fee not publicly listed; ask during consultation. ([iocdf.org](https://iocdf.org/providers/hart-john/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Andrea E. Kirby, PsyD — Dallas/Southlake area** | OCD-focused psychologist whose primary treatment is ERP; reported extensive OCD-specific training and experience at an OCD-specialty practice. Offers telehealth and self-pay. | Fee not publicly listed; confirm current availability and rate. ([olee-index.com](https://olee-index.com/provider/andrea-e-kirby?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Amiti Grozdon, M.Ed., LPC — Sagebrush Counseling** | Statewide Texas telehealth; trained in I-CBT and autistic-affirming ERP. Good option if you have rumination, obsessional doubt, or autism-related treatment needs. | **$200 for a 50–55 minute session**; $120 for a 30-minute check-in. ([sagebrushcounseling.com](https://www.sagebrushcounseling.com/ocd-therapist-texas?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Tina Smith, LPC — Ray of Hope Counseling** | 100% online across Texas and explicitly provides ERP for OCD and anxiety. | **$150 per 45–50 minute session**; private-pay clients can pay directly rather than use insurance. ([rohcounselingtx.com](https://www.rohcounselingtx.com/services/erp-therapy?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Lindy Noll, LCSW — Focus Integrated TX** | IOCDF-directory provider, BTTI-trained, offers virtual therapy to adults across Texas, including ERP and ACT-informed OCD treatment. | Fee not publicly listed; ask about self-pay and sliding scale. ([iocdf.org](https://iocdf.org/providers/noll-lindy/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Lukas Snear, LPC / Azimuth OCD and Anxiety** | OCD-specialty practice using ERP; listed as providing telehealth across Texas and treating OCD as an exclusive focus. | Reported private-pay rate around **$200/session**; supervised reduced-fee options are available through the practice. ([bdd.iocdf.org](https://bdd.iocdf.org/providers/snear-lukas/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Layers Counseling Specialists — Texas telehealth** | Private-pay group practice offering ERP for OCD, with clinicians licensed in Texas and online appointments statewide. | **$100–$250 per 50-minute session**, depending on clinician; some sliding-scale spots. ([layerscs.com](https://www.layerscs.com/locations/houston?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Steven Sainato, LPC — Dallas / Texas telehealth** | More budget-oriented option using ERP and ACT; works with adults and teens. | **$135/session** private pay; virtual sessions available in Texas. ([sainatocounseling.com](https://sainatocounseling.com/about?utm_source=openai)) |

### My practical shortlist

If you want the **most OCD-specialized/high-experience** options, I’d start with:

1. **John Hart, PhD**
2. **Andrea Kirby, PsyD**
3. **Lukas Snear / Azimuth**
4. **Amiti Grozdon**
5. **Lindy Noll**

If cost is a major factor, start with **Steven Sainato**, **Ray of Hope**, or ask Azimuth about its reduced-fee program. Azimuth advertises supervised telehealth sessions from **$40–$150**, depending on household income, though these are generally best suited to mild-to-moderate concerns. ([azimuthocd.com](https://www.azimuthocd.com/reduced-fee-counseling?utm_source=openai))

### Questions to ask before booking

You can send this:

> “I’m looking for private-pay telehealth treatment for OCD. How much of your practice involves OCD, and do you provide structured ERP—including exposure exercises and response-prevention homework? What is your session fee, cancellation policy, and availability? I do not want claims submitted to my insurance.”

Also ask:

- Do you treat **mental compulsions/rumination**, reassurance seeking, or “Pure O” presentations?
- Do you work with my specific subtype—scrupulosity, relationship OCD, health OCD, harm OCD, contamination, sexual intrusive thoughts, or sensorimotor OCD?
- Are you accepting new clients?
- Will you provide a **Good Faith Estimate**?
- Can you offer a sliding scale or shorter check-in sessions?

The IOCDF directory is also a good way to verify OCD-focused clinicians and filter specifically for teletherapy; it notes that listed providers’ licensure and relevant training are verified for directory inclusion. ([iocdf.org](https://iocdf.org/help/?utm_source=openai))
